subject: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: EdgeOps Support <edgeops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads

Hi team,

We observed repeated "gateway silence" from the customer private edge during two high-throughput upload windows this morning (08:05-08:10 and 08:40-08:43 PT). Symptoms:
- TCP sessions from customer instances to S3-backend time out mid-transfer; packets stop flowing for ~10-30s then resume.
- Traceroutes show path completion to the virtual gateway, but TCP dumps show SYN/ACK then long pause with no retransmits on the gateway side.
- We captured a short pcap and a traceroute (attached).

Initial guesses: MTU fragmentation+MSS-clamp mismatch or conntrack table exhaustion on the gateway under bursty NAT reuse (customer uses many short-lived outbound flows for uploads). Also seeing some ephemeral port reuse in the dump.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm whether the gateway conntrack table is hitting max during the bursts? If so, what's the current size and hashsize?
2) Any recent changes to port allocation, SNAT settings, or firewall session timeouts?
3) If conntrack is fine, please check kernel OOM/softnaptimeouts and any interface drops on the uplink.

Customer impact: uploads are failing ~15% of attempts during bursts; they're in a scheduled data-push and would like a mitigation ASAP.

I've opened INF-2309 and attached the captures. Will forward any additional logs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: pcap-snippet-20280209-08-13.cap (tcpdump), traces/20280209-vanessa-traceroute.txt (mtr/traceroute)

From: EdgeOps Support <edgeops@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-netops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads

Vanessa,

Thanks for the report and the captures. We pulled the gateway metrics for the time windows you listed. Quick findings:
- conntrack_count spikes coincide with the bursts and reaches ~96% of configured max (fn=262144 entries).
- conntrack_drop counter increments during the second window.
- No kernel OOMs; CPU and memory look nominal on the gateway.
- We see increases in retransmit counters on the external uplink during the pauses.

What we'll try immediately:
- Increase conntrack max to 524288 and bump hashsize per runbook.
- Enable MSS clamping on the NAT egress to 1400 to avoid large fragmented packets across the path.
- Temporarily extend TCP state timeouts for established flows to reduce churn while we monitor.

We'll apply the change to the customer's staging edge first and roll to prod if stable. Target ETA: 30-45 minutes. We'll post logs and a link to the rollout ticket.

—EdgeOps Support

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, EdgeOps Support <edgeops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads

Thanks for the quick triage. A couple of operational notes / hypotheses from our side:

1) Conntrack exhaustion + heavy SNAT port reuse is very plausible given short-lived outbound flows from the customer application. When conntrack is full, the kernel can start dropping new flow setups which manifests as silent stalls.
2) If NAT port exhaustion is the deeper issue, increasing conntrack alone won't fix it — we should also look at ephemeral port range (on the gateway) and whether the gw is doing 1:1 translation or port-based SNAT for many hosts behind it.
3) Another quick mitigation is to enable source-based NAT persistence (sticky SNAT) for the customer's upload hosts so flows reuse ports instead of creating high churn.

Suggested short-term rollout plan (staging -> prod):
- Increase conntrack_max and hashsize.
- Expand ephemeral port range to 32768-61000 on gateway.
- Apply MSS clamp 1400 on egress.
- Add a temporary conntrack timeout extension for CLOSE_WAIT->TIME_WAIT lowering churn (per runbook patch attached).

Connor: can you check whether the customer's edge is using a single SNAT IP or a pool? If single IP, we should prioritize ephemeral port expansion and consider adding SNAT IPs.

Karthik

From: EdgeOps Support <edgeops@acme-corp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-netops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads

Karthik / Vanessa,

Confirmed: prod edge is using a single SNAT IP for that tenant. We pushed the staging changes at 09:10: increased conntrack_max to 524288, expanded ephemeral range, and enabled MSS-clamp. Observed behavior on staging:
- conntrack_count stabilized; no drops in subsequent 20m of load test.
- No further silent pauses during high-burst synthetic uploads.

We plan a controlled rollout to prod at 09:50 PT with monitoring. We'll keep you posted. Creating INF-2309-ROLL1 and will link to the Jira.

—EdgeOps Support

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: EdgeOps Support <edgeops@acme-corp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Feb 2028 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private edge: intermittent gateway silence during high-burst uploads

Thanks — great work on the staging validation and fast rollout. Summary & next steps for ACME customer comms: 

- Root cause (working hypothesis): conntrack exhaustion + SNAT port packing on single public IP; MSS fragmentation amplified stalls for some flows.
- Short-term mitigation applied: conntrack_max doubling, ephemeral port range expansion, MSS clamp 1400, temporary timeout adjustments.
- Expected customer impact: should drop failure rate from ~15% to <1% for bursts.
- Medium-term follow-up: recommend adding a second SNAT IP and evaluate sticky SNAT for uploader hosts; update runbook to include port-pool scaling.

Marissa — please prepare a brief customer-facing note: what happened, what we changed, and the next plan (add SNAT IP / follow-up call). I'll join the call if they request immediate walk-through.

I'll attach the runbook patch and pcaps to the Jira. Thanks everyone for the rapid response.

Vanessa
